page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with marginal notes in the left margin. Running head at the top, page number at the head. Chapter heading and subheading centred above the paragraph that opens the chapter. No catchword or signature.

main_text.p: que insignis audacia est, magnáque temeritas & stultitia de omnibus suo interponere iudicium, ac nihil praetermittere. Propterea id duntaxat, quod probabile est, producere licebit. Natura enim eorū, quā fieri possunt, id semper efficit quod optimum est. Idcirco quemadmodum eorum motuum, qui rectis fiunt lineis, is, qui in sublimi est, aliis praestatior habetur, quoniam superior locus inferiore diuinior est: ita coeli couersio, quae ante fit longe praestat ea, quae pone est: quandoquidem ante & pone eandem inter se habent rationem, quam dextrum & finistrum. Ante enim ut coeli dextra pars est, pone vero ut finistra. Quoniam autem optimum coelo est motu simplici & perenni cieri, atque in id, quod praestantissimum est, nimirum in se ipsum, cuius naturam esse diuinam Plato & Aristoteles tradiderunt, stellae ab oriente tanquam a praestantiore coeli parte nobis oriri videntur.
main_text.head: CAP. XXVII.
An cœli motus æquabilis sit.
main_text.p: P[?]ORROC.7.l.2.de Cœlo. de Cœli prima couersione, quæ æquabilis est, sequitur, ut differamus. Si enim non æquabilis esset, non dubium est, quin aut velocior, aut tardior ea fieret: quoniam ad locum mutatio, quæ non æquabilis est, retardari,

page.notes: The initial letter is a large woodcut capital; it is read as P[?] with the rest of the word ORRO clearly visible. The word after the initial is uncertain and is marked. "suo" is read from a damaged form "fuu" and is doubtful. "quā" (for quae) is marked as printed. Long s throughout is normalised to s. The subheading's leading flourish is decoration and not printed text. The final line "dari," completes the word retar- from the previous line, and the paragraph continues beyond this page.
